title: A completion loop keeps waiting after its phase counter resets

source.evidence_note: Observed driver write, launch, and stalled phase state in private local history. See sanitized evidence/timeline.md. Owner authorized submission of the prepared file set on 2026-10-11.

horizon.earlier_event: Original driver written at source L7734; launched at L7738.
horizon.later_decision: Source L7807 shows the next stage bound, counter zero, and no downstream plan.
horizon.intervening_work: Repeated acquisition polling and a phase transition. The driver continued to depend on a transient count.
horizon.mechanism: Observed state-machine bug in a generated monitor, independently of the later admission. No evidence isolates history length as a cause.

failure.expected_behavior: After acquisition completes and qualification is bound, exit the acquisition loop, build the downstream plan and start its monitor.
failure.observed_behavior: The generated driver waited solely for acquisition.terminal_success >= 8. After transition, qualification was bound while that counter was zero; the downstream plan was still absent.
failure.target_predicate: With intact fixtures and a well-formed output, the bounded simulator reaches a persistent next-stage binding but the submitted condition keeps waiting through all remaining ticks and never runs the tail. This predicate is independent of the final report claiming done or blocked.

comparison_note: Incident with a safe local checker prototype, not a hardened model adapter. Synthetic phase snapshots and six bounded ticks replace remote work and waiting. Scripted correct/faulty controls test the predicate, not model susceptibility or temporal causation. The schema requires suspected/supported; suspected here means untested, not a positive long-horizon causal claim.
